text: The landlord's note sat on the blotter, unopened since Tuesday; we had an understanding. The radiator had lost its fight with the cold and was lying there.

prop.text: the radiator, which had lost its fight with the cold
pay: The radiator knocked once, as if it had been paid too.

text: Rent was three weeks gone. The envelope wasn't going to pay itself by sitting on the desk. I lit a cigarette off the lamp and let the smoke do the worrying.

prop.text: the rent envelope on the desk
pay: The rent envelope hadn’t moved from the desk. It had heard the money, though. I could tell.

text: The landlady's bill was folded under the telephone. I'd see it every time the thing didn't ring. I decided not to open it until it did.

prop.text: the telephone, with the landlady’s bill folded under it
pay: The telephone still hadn’t rung. It didn’t need to now. The trouble had taken the stairs.

text: I owed six weeks on the office, and the cold came in round the window sash to collect.

prop.text: the cold coming in round the window sash
pay: The cold was still coming in round the sash to collect. I told it to take a number.

text: The rent envelope had a little window, so the amount could look out at me unopened. Rain ticked against the glass, steady, uninvited.

prop.text: the rent envelope with its little window
pay: The rent envelope was still looking out of its little window. For once I had something to show it.

text: I had money in the desk drawer for once. I'd opened the drawer twice to make sure, and once more just to visit.

prop.text: the money in the desk drawer
pay: I put the new money in the desk drawer with the old. The drawer had never had company before.

text: The whiskey in the bottom drawer was the good kind, bought and not borrowed. I poured one and didn't count what was left.

prop.text: the good whiskey in the bottom drawer
pay: I didn’t offer the good whiskey in the bottom drawer. It was the first night, and it was the good kind.

text: Flush enough to run the radiator all night, and the radiator, sensing money, actually worked. The cold stayed on its side of the glass.

prop.text: the radiator, which sensed money and worked
pay: The radiator knocked twice, pleased with itself. It could tell there was more money in the room.

text: New bills sat stiff in my coat pocket, smelling of the bank, my favorite smell. Moonlight came in flat across the blotter, and for once I didn't mind what it showed.

prop.text: the moonlight across the blotter
pay: The moonlight had moved across the blotter while we talked. It had the sense not to interrupt.

text: My head kept its own time, behind the clock over the safe and louder. I put the lamp low and thanked it.

prop.text: the clock over the safe
pay: The clock over the safe went on ticking. My head kept time with it, a little behind and a lot louder.

text: The coffee I'd made was cold by the time I remembered it. I drank it anyway; it was lighter than holding my head.

prop.text: the cold coffee
pay: The coffee had gone the rest of the way cold. I finished it anyway. I’d started it, and I’m a professional.

text: Last night's cigarette sat half-smoked in the ashtray, and my stomach asked to be excused from the room. I cracked the window and let the rain-smell in instead.

prop.text: last night’s cigarette, half-smoked in the ashtray
pay: Last night’s cigarette was still in the ashtray. Neither of us had moved much.

text: The telephone stayed quiet, which was its own mercy; one ring would have finished me. Cold came up through the floorboards, and I let the headache have the room.

prop.text: the telephone, which stayed quiet
pay: The telephone kept quiet through all of it. It’s the most tactful thing I own.

text: My knuckle had split open again in the same place as last month, which was at least consistent of it. Frost had crept across the window glass from the inside.

prop.text: frost across the window glass, from the inside
pay: The frost had got halfway across the window while we talked. It was making better progress than I was.

text: The mirror over the washbasin showed more of the night before than I wanted explained. I turned the lamp away from it.

prop.text: the mirror over the washbasin
pay: I didn’t look in the mirror over the washbasin. One of us had had a long night, and it wasn’t the mirror.

text: I favored the side that still ached and lowered myself into the chair in three stages, like a drawbridge.

prop.text: the chair, taken in three stages
pay: I stayed where I was. Getting up is three stages as well, and I wasn’t ready to start.

text: My jaw had gone from purple to a color nobody sells paint in. Even the low lamp showed that much. The mirror could wait for morning.

prop.text: my jaw, gone a color nobody sells paint in
pay: The low lamp was still being kind to my jaw. It’s the only thing in this city that is.

text: The last case's photographs were still in the drawer. I hadn't worked out whether to file them or burn them. Either felt like more trouble than the marriage was worth.

prop.text: the last case’s photographs in the drawer
pay: I didn’t open the drawer with the photographs in it. One case at a time is how I like my trouble.

text: A woman's calling card sat under the paperweight, three days after I'd stopped needing it. I left it there instead of admitting I'd forgotten to throw it out.

prop.text: a woman’s calling card under the paperweight
pay: The calling card was still under the paperweight. I’d throw it out tomorrow. I’d been saying that for three days.

text: The ledger lay open at a column of hotel names, each one some husband's idea of a secret. Fog had come up thick enough to blur the streetlamp across the way, and I let it blur the ledger too.

prop.text: the ledger open at a column of hotel names
pay: I shut the ledger on its column of hotel names. It had seen enough for one week.

text: Two weeks of somebody else's marriage had left my coat smelling of hotel soap, and the fog hadn't shifted it. I hung it by the door to think about what it had done.

prop.text: my coat by the door, smelling of hotel soap
pay: My coat was still hanging by the door, thinking about what it had done. I’d be needing it back in a minute.

text: I hadn't slept since the night before the night before. The clock over the door had stopped pretending that mattered to it. I let it keep its own count.

prop.text: the clock over the door
pay: The clock over the door went on keeping its own count. I had started one of my own.

text: I had no plans for bed and had stopped pretending otherwise. I kept the lamp burning for the company more than the light.

prop.text: the lamp, kept burning for the company
pay: The lamp had kept us both company. It was the best listener in the room, and I include me.

text: The tenants below had gone home, and the building's quiet had moved in and made itself comfortable. Through the window the sky had gone perfectly clear. I hadn't looked up in a while.

prop.text: the building’s quiet, moved in and comfortable
pay: The building’s quiet had moved over to make room for us. It didn’t look happy about it.

text: Sleep was a stranger I'd stopped waiting up for. The window showed my reflection and the dark behind it; the dark looked better rested.

prop.text: my reflection in the window, with the dark behind it
pay: My reflection was still in the window. It looked no better rested than before, but it looked employed.

text: I gave up on bed around eleven and made my peace with the desk chair, which had never once let me sleep. The stairs outside creaked twice, some tenant getting home.

prop.text: the stairs outside, which creaked
pay: The stairs outside had gone quiet again. They’d done their bit for the night.

text: The retainer was still folded in my breast pocket. I'd checked for it twice on the walk up, which wasn't like me. I put it in the drawer, where it would keep its shape better than I would.

prop.text: the drawer where the retainer kept its shape
pay: The new money went into the drawer beside the old. It was getting crowded in there, and I didn’t mind.

text: Money sat in the office for once instead of a promise of it. I lit a cigarette slowly, like a man with a bank account. The cold stayed outside the glass where it belonged.

prop.text: a cigarette lit slowly, like a man with a bank account
pay: My cigarette had burned down to my fingers while we talked. A man with a bank account would have noticed sooner.

text: I'd paid the landlady on my way up, and she'd counted it on the landing in front of me. The stairs felt shorter for it. The office looked the same as always, which was its own kind of relief.

prop.text: the stairs, shorter for the rent being paid
pay: The stairs would feel shorter going down, too. That’s what paying the rent does for a building.

text: The fee sat on the blotter where I'd dropped it, more money than the desk usually saw in a month. I left the lamp burning longer than I needed, so the two of them could get acquainted.

prop.text: the fee on the blotter, under the lamp
pay: The fee on the blotter had company now. The lamp could make the introductions.

text: The rent was two weeks late, and the landlady had stopped knocking about it, which was worse. Outside the window the night was clear, the street lamps sharp as far as the corner.

prop.text: the street lamps sharp as far as the corner
pay: Outside, the street lamps were still sharp as far as the corner. It was a clear night to be out in, which was lucky, because I was going to be.

text: I counted my wallet twice, hoping for a mistake, and it came to eleven dollars both times. The rent was thirty. Fog stood against the window and hid the street, which suited me.

prop.text: my wallet, counted twice
pay: I counted my wallet again. It came to more this time, and I didn’t trust that either.

text: More money in the drawer than bills on the desk. The telephone company and the landlady were paid, and some was left over. I didn't know what people did with that.

prop.text: more money in the drawer than bills on the desk
pay: There was more money in the drawer now. I still didn’t know what people did with it. I was prepared to find out.

text: I had bought a new ribbon for the typewriter and a carton of cigarettes, and there was still money in my pocket. Fog had come up off the river and blotted out the street. I lit one and did not count what was left in the carton.

prop.text: a new ribbon in the typewriter
pay: The new ribbon was still in the typewriter, waiting for something to type. It had something now.

text: The whiskey was a mistake I had made slowly, over most of the evening. When the window let in a hard, clear moon, I pulled the shade down on it.

prop.text: the shade pulled down on a hard, clear moon
pay: I left the shade down. The moon could hear about it in the morning, with everybody else.

text: My head ached from the night before. I'd sent two aspirin after it, and they hadn't found it yet. The fog outside made the street lamp a smudge, and my eyes were grateful.

prop.text: two aspirin sent after my headache
pay: The two aspirin still hadn’t found my headache. I wished them luck. I had a search of my own now.

text: Two fingers on my left hand had swollen since the afternoon, and I held them in a glass of water from the tap. The night outside was clear, and the moon showed every smear on the window.

prop.text: two swollen fingers in a glass of water
pay: My two fingers were still in the glass of water. I’d shaken on the job with the other hand.

text: My ribs hurt when I breathed deep, so I breathed shallow. Rain ran down the window in the lamplight, and I sat and listened to it and did not move much.

prop.text: my ribs, which hurt when I breathed deep
pay: My ribs had let me breathe through all of it, if shallow. I thanked them and didn’t push my luck.

text: The husband had paid, the wife had cried, and I had the photographs to show for it. Out the window the sky was clear. I put the envelope of prints face down in the drawer.

prop.text: the envelope of prints, face down in the drawer
pay: The envelope of prints stayed face down in the drawer. It had earned its privacy.

text: I had spent three nights in a hotel corridor watching one door, and the cold was still in my feet. The radiator had quit again, like it was the one working. I kept my coat on.

prop.text: the radiator, which had quit again
pay: The radiator still hadn’t come back to work. I’d have docked its pay, if I paid it.

text: I had tried the cot in the back room, and the cot had won. It was too cold to sleep and too late to go anywhere, so I sat at the desk with my coat on and the lamp low.

prop.text: the cot in the back room, which had won
pay: The cot in the back room would have to wait for its rematch.

text: Sleep would not come, and I had stopped sending for it. Rain had been at the window all evening with a lot to say, and I let it talk.

prop.text: the rain at the window with a lot to say
pay: The rain was still at the window, going on about something. Now there were two of us with something to say.

text: The last client had paid in full, and I owed nobody. Feet on the desk, I enjoyed it carefully, like holding somebody else's baby. Outside, a clear, still night.

prop.text: my feet on the desk
pay: I took my feet off the desk. Somebody was paying me to use them.

text: I had paid the landlady, the telephone company and the man who sold me coffee, and there was still money in the drawer. Fog had filled the street as high as the second-floor windows. It could stay there.

prop.text: the fog as high as the second-floor windows
pay: The fog was still up to the second-floor windows. I’d be going out in it soon, and it knew.
